title: Reading Conversational Tone from KV-Cache Keys
subtitle: Position and Planning-Text Confounds (A Methods Note)
abstract: This methods note reports what one instrument can and cannot see of conversational tone: cached keys projected on emotion directions at four early full-attention layers. Its readings are dominated by sequence position, far more than by the tone compared. In Experiment 1 the chunk-average reading (user, assistant and probe tokens mixed) falls from +4.75 and +4.22 (cheerful, hostile) at one emotional turn to +0.44 and -0.34 at eight, against a gap of 0.53 to 0.78 between arms; position is not separated from the amount of history. The stored assistant turns are the model's planning text, which often names the user's tone (in Experiment 1, 59 of 135 hostile-arm and 54 of 135 cheerful-arm excerpts), so readings of history contain the model's own written labels, except where the chat template stripped the planning. Experiment 1 cannot test accumulation: its arms differ in text at every read site. Experiment 2's arms differ in text at the measured turn, and its comparisons between them are withdrawn. The one length-matched comparison, hostile against cheerful persona prompts, moves valence (d_av = -0.68) consistently on five probes, too few to reach p < 0.05 by permutation; its script is not shipped. A test would need fixed (teacher-forced) neutral assistant turns, the recurrent layers read turn by turn, position-matched or de-rotated keys, and behavior as ground truth.
